intro.author: 'The elder' (v. 1), traditionally the apostle John; some scholars think it was another church leader known as John the Elder
intro.written: Probably about AD 85–95, around the time of 1 and 2 John
intro.audience: Gaius, a believer the elder loved and praised for his hospitality (v. 1); Gaius was a common name, and he cannot be identified with others of that name in the New Testament
intro.setting: Traveling missionaries relied on local believers for food and lodging. Gaius had welcomed them, but Diotrephes, a leader 'who loveth to have the preeminence' (v. 9), refused to receive them or the elder's earlier letter and even put out of the church those who did. Demetrius, who probably carried this letter, is warmly recommended (v. 12).
intro.purpose: The elder commends Gaius, urges him to keep supporting faithful missionaries, rebukes the conduct of Diotrephes, and recommends Demetrius.
intro.bigIdea: Those who support people who serve the truth become fellow workers with the truth.
